page: Amazon Web Services m3.medium is a general-purpose, third-generation virtual machine instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 4.0 GB of system memory, a 25 MB L3 cache, and hardware support for AVX and AES instructions. Local storage is provided via a bundled 4 GB NVMe SSD, while the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations position the m3.medium in the lower performance tiers. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests yield identical scores of 1259.98, reflecting the single-threaded hardware limitation. Memory performance is constrained, with large-block read and write bandwidths measuring 11.78 GB/sec and 10.36 GB/sec, respectively. Geekbench testing reports a single-core score of 668.0 and a multi-core score of 669.0, placing the instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware.

Given its hardware profile, the m3.medium is suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic text processing, simple static web serving, or minor database operations. It is not designed for parallelized computing, large-scale software compilation, or modern LLM inference. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a low-resource entry point with dedicated CPU allocation, though its older architecture and low benchmark-per-resource density limit its utility for modern production environments.

Benchmark results place this instance in the lower percentiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 668.0 and a multi-core score of 669.0. Memory bandwidth is limited, reaching 11.78 GB/sec for large-block reads.
